body:
## STACK-ECONOMICS REPORT (axis 7: 스택·배포·비용)

Scope: greenfield AI presentation-agent PWA, 5 students, 500,000 KRW (~US$365) total budget, 2026.6~2027.3, ~10 concurrent demo users (from 신청서). All prices verified from vendor pricing pages fetched 2026-08-13 (sources inline). Verdict up front: **the binding constraint is engineering time, not money — a $0/month infra stack is not just possible, it is the correct answer; the proposed budget line for ChatGPT subscriptions (~477,000 KRW) is 10-40x what API usage will cost.**

### 1. Component comparison (MVP = what to build; PROD = what to grow into, ~$30-60/mo, NOT before demo)

**PWA framework** — MVP: Vite + React + TypeScript SPA + vite-plugin-pwa (or SvelteKit). PROD: same. Next.js SSR adds zero value here: app is behind auth (no SEO), two views (presenter console / audience screen) are routes + BroadcastChannel. PWA needs only HTTPS + manifest + SW — free on any static host. Multi-window/display handling is a browser API problem (Window Management API), orthogonal to framework. Do not add a PWA framework layer (e.g., no Workbox manual config; vite-plugin-pwa suffices).
**Backend** — MVP: Supabase Edge Functions (TS/Deno) + Supabase Auth. Evidence: free tier = 500K edge invocations/mo, unlimited API requests, no CPU-time cap (supabase.com/pricing). PROD: same, or move orchestrator to Vercel Pro ($20/mo) if team prefers Next.js server functions. Reject Cloudflare Workers free for the orchestrator: 10ms CPU/invocation cap (developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing) is genuinely tight for prompt assembly + JWT verify + JSON handling in a 5s SLA pipeline.
**DB** — MVP: Supabase Postgres free (500MB, 2 projects, pauses after 1 week inactivity — supabase.com/pricing). PROD: Supabase Pro $25/mo (8GB). Alternative D1 (5GB free, 5M rows read/day) is fine for plain relational but has no vector search → loses on RAG.
**Realtime** — MVP: Supabase Realtime (free: 200 concurrent connections, 2M messages/mo — ~40x headroom at 10 users). This is the only realtime need: session state, card state machine, transcript, team messages — all small JSON. PROD: same (500 conns on Pro). WebRTC rejected: no audience audio/video streaming in spec. Pusher/Ably free tiers (100 conns) exist but add a 4th vendor for zero benefit.
**Object storage** — MVP: Supabase Storage (1GB free, RLS policies — security win: ACL'd deck serving via Postgres policies). PROD: Cloudflare R2 (10GB free, $0.015/GB, **free egress** — developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing). Decks are 5-50MB; 1GB covers ~20-100 decks. Also: do NOT store raw presentation audio (privacy + storage cost); transcript-only.
**Vector/search** — MVP: **pgvector in Supabase Postgres (free, no extra vendor)**. Scale: <10K chunks (deck corpus) — pgvector HNSW is 100x overkill-headroom. Evidence-based decision: Cloudflare Vectorize is *"currently only available on the Workers paid plan"* per current docs (free column with 30M queried/5M stored dims appears contradictory — LEAD 2). PROD: stay on pgvector; Pinecone/Weaviate only at >1M chunks. Lexical+dense hybrid: Postgres FTS (tsvector) + pgvector, merge in the edge function.
**STT** — MVP: **Deepgram Nova-3, `language=ko`**, streaming WSS direct from browser (key via short-lived backend token; or server-side socket). Evidence: ko/ko-KR supported on nova-3 streaming (developers.deepgram.com/docs/models-languages-overview); streaming promo $0.0048/min mono / $0.0058/min multilingual, **$200 free credit** (deepgram.com/pricing) ≈ 41,000+ minutes — covers the entire project. **CRITICAL: new Flux model does NOT support Korean** — do not pick Flux. PROD: same. Alternatives: OpenAI gpt-4o-mini-transcribe $0.003/min but batch-oriented; gpt-live-transcribe $0.017/min streaming is 3.5x Deepgram promo (platform.openai.com/docs/pricing); Whisper $0.006/min batch-only; Naver Clova/Vito = Korean-native fallback if Nova-3 Korean accuracy disappoints (benchmark day — LEAD 3).
**LLM/VLM** — MVP: gpt-5-mini ($0.25/$2.00 per 1M tokens) for synthesis; gpt-5-nano ($0.05/$0.40) only for trivial classification after quality check; gpt-4o-mini ($0.15/$0.60) or gpt-5.4-mini for per-slide VLM analysis; text-embedding-3-small ($0.02/1M tokens) for dense vectors. Cost math below shows ~$1-10 total. PROD: same; add prompt caching (cached input $0.025/M on gpt-5-mini) for the 5s SLA.
**Observability** — MVP: **PostHog free** (1M events, 100K exceptions, 5K session recordings, 10GB logs, 1 project — posthog.com/pricing) = analytics + error tracking + session replay in one. Plus platform logs (Cloudflare Workers Logs 200K events/day 3-day retention, or Vercel runtime logs 1h on Hobby). PROD: PostHog pay-as-you-go or Sentry team ($26/mo). Reject: Grafana/Prometheus/self-hosted, Datadog, 3-vendor observability stacks. Sentry free now = 1 user, 5GB logs (sentry.io/pricing); error quota unclear → LEAD 4 (don't run both PostHog and Sentry).

### 2. Deployment topology

**MVP ($0/mo infra):** Static PWA (audience view + console) on Cloudflare Pages or Vercel Hobby → Supabase Free (Postgres+pgvector+Realtime+Storage+Auth+Edge Functions) → Deepgram (STT, credit) + OpenAI API (LLM). 3 vendors total. Domain optional (~15,000 KRW/yr); *.pages.dev/*.vercel.app is PWA-valid (HTTPS + SW work).
**PROD (~$30-60/mo):** Same topology + Vercel Pro ($20) or Workers Paid ($5) + Supabase Pro ($25) + domain. Trigger: >10K MAU, multi-tenant, or need of backups/SLA. Not needed for competition demo.
**Rejected:** VPS self-host (Hetzner ~€4/mo — ops burden, no advantage at this scale), Korean-cloud hosting (Naver/Kakao — only worth it for Korean STT specifically), Kubernetes/containers (serverless only), microservices.

### 3. 9-month cost model (evidence-based)

| Item | MVP cost | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Infra (hosting/DB/realtime/storage/vector) | $0 | supabase.com/pricing, cloudflare.com pricing |
| STT: 20 talks × 30min = 600 min × $0.0048 | ~$3 (covered by $200 credit) | deepgram.com/pricing |
| LLM: 600 confirmed-utterance calls × ~2.4K tokens | ~$1 | platform.openai.com/docs/pricing |
| VLM: 400 slide analyses (gpt-4o-mini) | ~$1 | same |
| Embeddings: 10K chunks | <$1 | same |
| Observability | $0 | posthog.com/pricing |
| Domain (optional) | ~$15 | market |
| **Total 9 months** | **~$5-20 (~10-25K KRW)** | |
| Worst case (10x testing volume) | <$100 | |

→ Compare: proposed ChatGPT subscription allocation ~477,000 KRW. **Recommendation: reallocate to API credit buffer (100-200K KRW cap via hard spend limits) + domain; surplus stays unspent.** Every vendor above supports hard spend caps/budgets except free tiers (which hard-stop at limits).

### 4. Build sequence (8 weeks, MVP-first; each stage demoable)

1. Wk1-2: Deck upload → parse (python-pptx for PPTX; pdf.js/pdftotext for PDF — where python runs is LEAD 6) → slide registry (deck_id, slide_id, version) + chunk + embed → pgvector. 
2. Wk2-3: Streaming STT (Deepgram WSS → transcript events with timestamps → Realtime channel).
3. Wk3-4: Event orchestrator (edge fn): confirmed-utterance → event-driven search/RAG/LLM (NOT continuous) → card state machine (SUPPORTED/UNCERTAIN/CONFLICTING/UNSUPPORTED/STALE/SUPERSEDED) → audience-safe channel only for SUPPORTED.
4. Wk4-5: Two-view split: extended display (Window Management API, one gesture) + clone display (2nd device, session sync via Realtime). Failure drill: network loss mid-talk.
5. Wk5-6: ACL prefilter + revision/anchor/content-hash verification; cooldown; 5s-SLA tuning (prompt caching, parallel search, pre-warm per-slide).
6. Wk6-7: Post-presentation report = SQL event replay (no extra infra).
7. Wk7-8: PostHog wiring, spend caps, demo hardening (Supabase wake-up protocol!).

### 5. Ruthless cuts (explicit "do not build")
No Redis (cooldown = Postgres column; Upstash free 256MB/500K cmd only if profiling shows need), no queue/Kafka (Postgres-backed retry table), no dedicated vector DB, no WebRTC, no SSR, no microservices, no Terraform, no self-hosted monitoring, no raw-audio storage, no realtime presence infra beyond Realtime, no CI beyond GitHub Actions deploy-on-push.

### 6. LEADS (raised immediately)
1. **5s SLA is the binding constraint, not cost** — latency budget: STT finalize ~200-500ms + hybrid search <500ms + gpt-5-mini ~1-3s. Verify with real Korean audio; pre-warming + prompt caching are the levers. Coordinate with realtime-ai.
2. **Cloudflare Vectorize docs contradiction**: page states "currently only available on the Workers paid plan" yet tabulates a free tier (30M queried/5M stored dims/mo). Verify before any Cloudflare-native RAG path; pgvector makes this moot for MVP.
3. **Deepgram Nova-3 Korean accuracy unverified** — ko is officially supported; Flux is NOT (10 langs only). Budget one benchmark day vs Naver Clova/Vito; Nova-3 keyterm prompting ($0.0013/min) can boost domain jargon.
4. **Sentry free tier changed** (1 user, unlimited projects, 5GB logs); per-error quota not shown on fetched page — verify if Sentry chosen; prefer PostHog (100K exceptions free) to avoid dual vendors.
5. **Supabase free project pauses after 1 week inactivity** — demo-day risk. Mitigation: weekly keep-alive cron (Cloudflare cron is free) or documented 60s wake; rehearse the wake path pre-demo. Also free tier = 1-day log retention (debugging friction).
6. **python-pptx runtime location** (spec lists it): PPTX parsing is Python-only server-side work — options: local dev-machine script on upload (MVP), Supabase Edge Functions can't run Python, or free Render/Cloud Run worker (PROD). Needs a decision from backend owner.
7. **Vercel Hobby = 1 developer seat + personal/non-commercial** — a 5-student team cannot all deploy; Cloudflare Pages has no seat limit, or use GH Actions deploy. Verify team workflow early.
8. **Workers free 10ms CPU cap** makes Cloudflare-native orchestration risky (LEAD 1 interaction); if Path B is chosen anyway, budget $5/mo paid plan.
9. **Supabase region for Korea**: nearest region is Tokyo (no Seoul region as of fetch date) — verify; DB round-trip latency ~30-60ms from Seoul, acceptable for 5s SLA.
10. **Raw audio privacy**: spec's security axis implies no raw audio persistence; transcript-only storage also saves cost — confirm with security-privacy.
11. **Spend guardrails**: free tiers hard-stop (good); any paid upgrade must set hard spend caps — one rogue demo could otherwise burn the 500K KRW on API overage.

## EXPAND
- Verify Naver Clova Speech / Vito / ETRI streaming Korean STT pricing + accuracy vs Deepgram Nova-3 with a recorded Korean sample (cost/accuracy tradeoff table for the report).
- Verify Supabase Seoul-adjacent region list + Tokyo latency and free-tier wake latency from Korea.
- Pull current GPT API credit minimum purchase (OpenAI prepaid) and whether Korean credit cards work — a real onboarding blocker for Korean students.
- Cost-sensitivity table: production-ready path month-by-month for 6 months post-demo (Vercel Pro + Supabase Pro + PostHog paid) to size the "if it survives the competition" budget ask.
- Quantify LLM cost per talk with gpt-5-nano vs gpt-5-mini on card classification quality (needs a labeled sample — coordinate with realtime-ai).
- Confirm whether Supabase Storage free 50MB max upload size limits deck ingestion (decks 5-50MB — borderline; RLS + size check needed).
summary: Stack-economics report: $0/mo MVP stack, evidence-backed cost model, build sequence
